teams.synopsis: One of the most dominant stretches in PFFL history — 150+ points a week for a month, led by the league's best fantasy player.
teams.blurb: Charlie's team stands out as one of the most dominant forces in PFFL history, despite not having the best regular-season record. What sets this team apart is its exceptional point-scoring performance, consistently averaging over 150 points per week over the past four weeks. This consistency propels Charlie to the top spot in the final rankings, making him the frontrunner for the 2023 PFFL Championship. The team's success is anchored by the standout fantasy player of the year, Tyreek Hill, complemented by a roster filled with top-15 players at every position. Anticipating matchups against other formidable teams like Baylen and Carmine, Charlie's team is poised to be a major player in the playoffs, capable of taking down any other top contender.

teams.synopsis: The 2nd-best record and the most total points in the league — but stuck on the same playoff bracket side as Charlie.
teams.blurb: Carmine's team has consistently earned its place among the top three teams in the league throughout the season, a reputation solidified by finishing with the second-best record and the highest total points. The team is led by the best quarterback in fantasy and the second-best tight end, and with running backs and wide receivers possessing top-10 weekly upside, Carmine's roster is well-rounded and formidable. The challenge lies in the playoff bracket, where Carmine finds himself on the same side as Charlie, the only team ranked above him to close out the season. Overcoming that obstacle will be crucial for a deep playoff run and a shot at a first PFFL Championship.

teams.synopsis: A strong 4th-seed season now clouded by injuries to all three of his top backs right as the playoffs begin.
teams.blurb: Brandon's team has been a strong contender throughout the season, securing the 4th seed as the playoffs approach. However, recent injuries to key players like <mark class="hl-player">Jonathan Taylor</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Josh Jacobs</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Isiah Pacheco</mark> have raised concerns about their availability for Round 1, making the matchup against Cole more unpredictable. Despite the challenges, Brandon's team has demonstrated resilience throughout the season, and if it can navigate through these injuries successfully, it still has the potential to be a formidable force in the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: A first-ever winning season, and the rarest kind — zero trades all year, same as Charlie and 2021-champion Ben.
teams.blurb: Throughout most of the season, Cole's performance deviated from his typical patterns, especially leading up to Week 14. Historically prone to frequent injuries, this season saw a remarkable scarcity of them — though that didn't hold all the way through, as <mark class="hl-player">Keenan Allen</mark>'s unavailability for Week 15 has compelled Cole to start <mark class="hl-player">Ty Chandler</mark> at flex. The upcoming matchup against Brandon's team, currently without its top three running backs, adds an intriguing dimension. Reflecting on the whole season, Cole's team achieved a positive record for the first time in franchise history — all while abstaining from any trades, a decision shared by only two other teams ever: Charlie and Ben's 2021 squad, which went on to win that year's championship.

teams.synopsis: A streaky season that still landed a playoff berth — Dak, Etienne, and Kelce lead a roster built for one more win streak.
teams.blurb: Aidan's team began the season with a robust 3-1 record, albeit without points production that fully justified it. A second 3-1 surge from Week 5 to Week 8 showed real improvement, averaging 136 points per game. Despite a downturn to 1-5 in the weeks that followed, Aidan's team still secured a berth in the 2023 PFFL Playoffs. The team is led by Dak Prescott, Travis Etienne, and Travis Kelce, complemented by solid contributors like Tyler Lockett, Najee Harris, and Terry McLaurin, with Chris Olave teetering on the edge of WR1 status all year. Despite a projected deficit of over 20 points, a first-round win over Carmine could make this team a real threat.

teams.synopsis: From a 57-point punchline in Week 1 to a real playoff berth — Moss, Chase, LaPorta, Stroud, and Thielen carried the turnaround.
teams.blurb: The inaugural week of the season presented a challenging start for Baylen's team, posting a mere 57 points — an outcome that positioned Baylen as a potential subject of amusement in the 2023 PFFL. A resilient and impressive season subsequently unfolded, though, culminating in a playoff berth that defied the earlier skepticism. Notable contributors included Zach Moss, Ja'Marr Chase, Sam LaPorta, CJ Stroud, and Adam Thielen, each making significant impacts at various points. Facing a formidable opponent in the first round, Baylen's team must overcome the odds for a chance to propel the franchise into its first-ever championship run — an upset over Charlie's team could serve as the momentum catalyst for a deeper run.

teams.synopsis: A dominant first 10 weeks derailed by injuries to Andrews, Dell, and Herbert — the playoffs will test the depth that's left.
teams.blurb: As I pen the final rankings for the 2023 season, the spotlight is not on my own team ascending to the top spot. Ethan's team emerged as a dominant force in the initial 10 weeks of the season, showcasing remarkable prowess. However, a turn of misfortune in the form of injuries to key players such as <mark class="hl-player">Mark Andrews</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Tank Dell</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Justin Herbert</mark> has cast a shadow over the potential for a championship run. The challenge now is whether this resilient team can overcome that adversity and still secure victories in the playoffs. Looking forward to 2024, there's optimism coupled with a determination to avoid a repeat of 2023's breakdowns.

teams.synopsis: A Week 14 win locks in a 7-7 playoff berth — but a tough Week 15 draw makes the path forward uncertain.
teams.blurb: A thrilling victory in Week 14 secured a coveted spot for Ryan's team in the 2023 PFFL Playoffs. However, looming questions surround the team's potential for a championship run. Reflecting on the season, it's evident that Ryan's running backs played a pivotal role, with recent performances from DeAndre Hopkins and Trey McBride contributing to the team's 7-7 record. Facing Week 15 with less favorable matchups and uncertainty around Nico Collins's availability, the outlook is challenging — Ryan's team may need significant help to extend its playoff journey.

teams.synopsis: The first-ever missed playoffs for the defending champ — elite names at the top, but never enough support around them.
teams.blurb: The defending PFFL Champion's lackluster season concluded with a notably dramatic exit from playoff contention last week — the first time in PFFL history that Anthony failed to secure a spot in the playoffs. Throughout the season, the team lacked a true standout, with the RB8 emerging as the de facto MVP. Despite possessing formidable talents in the likes of <mark class="hl-player">Justin Jefferson</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Stefon Diggs</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Bijan Robinson</mark>, this season never gave the team a real chance to pursue another PFFL Championship. Looking ahead, Anthony is poised for a more promising 2024 campaign, with the offseason likely a critical period for strategic adjustments.

teams.synopsis: A slow start, then a late-season rally that kept the 'failure' label off the door — Gibbs and DJ Moore lead into 2024.
teams.blurb: Max's team experienced a distinctive journey in the 2023 season, prompting reflections on whether it could replicate the playoff success achieved in 2020. The first half of the season seemed to cast doubt on that prospect, but as the team rallied toward the end, a league-wide realization emerged that any team under Max's management retains the potential for a postseason surge. Key contributors this year included <mark class="hl-player">Jahmyr Gibbs</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">DJ Moore</mark>, both of whom showcased exciting play and are likely centerpieces for Max in 2024. While the overall performance exhibited inconsistencies, the late-season resurgence prevented the season from being unequivocally deemed a failure.

teams.synopsis: A middling season despite real RB talent — Montgomery and Achane both averaged 16+, but injuries got in the way.
teams.blurb: Throughout the course of this year, Deniz's team experienced its fair share of highs and lows, ultimately concluding on a somewhat disappointing note. Since their last deep playoff run in 2020, the team has struggled to regain that level of success, a trend set to persist into 2024. Despite possessing considerable talent this season — exemplified by the impressive performances of running backs Montgomery and Achane, both averaging over 16 points per game — their potential was hindered by a series of unfortunate injuries. The 2023 season can be characterized as middling, with the team's journey concluding in a manner consistent with its overall performance.

teams.synopsis: The Nick Chubb injury reshaped the whole season — Puka Nacua's emergence is the clearest silver lining.
teams.blurb: Andrew's 2023 season faced a significant setback when Nick Chubb suffered an injury, marking a turning point that had a profound impact on the team's performance. Despite the strategic decision to prioritize a formidable running back duo, the unfortunate separation of that pair dealt a blow to the team's aspirations. Notably, Puka Nacua emerged as a bright spot, currently holding the WR10 position and offering promise for continued excellence even in the absence of a playoff berth. Reflecting on the season, Andrew's team lacked an elite-caliber player, falling short of the caliber represented by Josh Jacobs in the previous year. The absence of NY Routensss from the playoffs marks a noteworthy deviation from league history, introducing an element of novelty as new teams vie for greatness.

teams.synopsis: Called 'unlucky' early, but the season's arc revealed real underperformance — Mostert was the lone bright spot.
teams.blurb: A season that commenced with the label of 'unlucky' ultimately validated such characterization for Ben's team. While initially ascribed to challenging losses in the opening month, the narrative evolved over the subsequent two months, revealing a team plagued by consistent underperformance rather than mere misfortune. Despite the unexpected emergence of <mark class="hl-player">Raheem Mostert</mark> as a standout player, the remainder of Ben's roster struggled to deliver consistent contributions. Mostert's elite production served as a bright spot amid an otherwise lackluster performance. Looking forward, the league awaits Ben's potential resurgence in 2024, curious whether his 2021 championship run was a repeatable feat or an isolated occurrence.

teams.synopsis: A draft-day hole at RB1 and no top-20 WR ever really recovered — a 2-12 season with real cause.
teams.blurb: Persistently characterized as the league's underperforming outfit, Quin's team endured a notably disappointing 2023 season. The primary source of this team's struggles consistently traces back to its draft performance — Quin failed to secure impactful picks, evident in the selection of the RB22 in the first round and the absence of any top-20 wide receiver from the draft. The 2-12 record underscores the considerable room for improvement across the roster. However, this challenging season could serve as a catalyst for a significant resurgence in 2024, a year Quin approaches with a relatively unburdened outlook. The upcoming offseason presents a valuable opportunity to address these deficiencies and stage a compelling comeback, potentially culminating in a run at the 2024 PFFL Playoffs.
